thread:
sasha: Heads up — customers hitting a crash when using the JS SDK from Next.js middleware (runtime: 'edge'). Build fails with 'ReferenceError: require is not defined' and also TypeScript complaining about missing types for subpath imports.

sasha: Minimal middleware repro we tried:
```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
export default function middleware(req) {
  const c = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
  return NextResponse.next()
}
```

sasha: Build error from Vercel preview: 
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at Object.<anonymous> (dist/index.cjs:1:20)
    at __webpack_require__ (bootstrap:25:1)
```

nate: Sounds like bundler resolving the CJS main entry despite there being an esm build. Edge needs pure ESM and no node builtins (process, fs, Buffer, node:crypto). Do we have conditional exports in package.json?

sasha: package.json currently: "main": "dist/index.cjs", "module": "dist/index.esm.js", "types": "dist/index.d.ts". There's an old `browser` field but bundler still picks main for middleware.

julie: Next/Edge bundler can prefer `main`. Add an explicit `exports` map with an edge-specific subpath. Example suggestion:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

julie: Also publish a tiny `dist/edge` build that avoids Node-only APIs. For crypto, either use globalThis.crypto.subtle (Web Crypto) or provide a small runtime wrapper that picks the right API.

nate: Quick user workaround: `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk/edge'` if we publish that path. But TS needs types for the subpath.

sasha: I tried that locally by symlinking a built edge folder into node_modules and importing `redwood-sdk/edge` — it built, but TypeScript error: `Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood-sdk/edge'`.

julie: So we must include `.d.ts` artifacts in dist/edge and reference them in exports. Also update `types` or ship `types` per subpath in exports.

nate: I'll open a PR with these changes: 1) add an edge build target in our bundler config (emit ESM .mjs files under dist/edge), 2) conditional exports including `./edge`, 3) edge typings `dist/edge/index.d.ts`, 4) example under `examples/next-edge-middleware` and a CI job that does an edge-compat build check.

sasha: Thanks. Can we also add a small README snippet listing Edge constraints so users don't attempt to use node builtins? Short checklist to add to README: no sync fs, no child_process, use fetch, use Web Crypto, avoid Buffer without polyfill.

julie: Yep. Also adjust our published type declarations to avoid referencing Node global types (process, Buffer) in the ambient index.d.ts — those break projects compiled for lib:dom or edge runtimes. Make types conditional or create separate edge index.d.ts that only references DOM types.

sasha: Filed a DX bug for that. The root index.d.ts had `declare const process: NodeJS.Process` in one spot which forces Node types.

nate: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/495 — includes edge bundle, exports map, edge types, example app, and a changelog entry. CI now runs `pnpm build:edge` and a tiny script that uses esbuild to ensure no node: builtin imports remain.

sasha: Pulled the PR into a preview build and the middleware error is gone 389. Vercel preview: https://vercel.app/preview/next-edge-sdk-fix (deployed). Example middleware now imports `redwood-sdk/edge` and runs in preview.

docs-bot: Note added to docs backlog: "Next Edge import pattern + runtime constraints" — assigned to docs team.

julie: Follow-ups: Nate 0 add a one-paragraph migration note in CHANGELOG explaining `./edge` path and why it exists. Sasha 0 sanity-check the example for minimum APIs and typings. I'll add an automated test that imports the edge path in a TS project configured for `lib: ['dom']` and asserts the compiler doesn't need Node types.

sasha: Will do. Also fixed one more thing — we had a `Buffer` type leakage in a type alias which I removed in the edge d.ts. That resolved TS errors in Next Edge projects.

nate: After merge we'll cut a patch release and add the example to the docs site and `examples/` index. Also add a short troubleshooting snippet: "If you see 'require is not defined', ensure you import the edge entry or upgrade to SDK >= x.y.z."

sasha: Great. This will unblock customers using middleware + edge functions. Thanks! :thumbsup:
